DISCOVER MARIN’S SECRET SPOTS WITH SPECTACULAR VIEWS AND COASTAL VISTAS –SURPRISES EVERYWHERE YOU LOOK!

By
-
November 2, 2026
0
739
Facebook

    https://www.visitmarin.org/media/marin-video/culinary-branding-videos

    Listen to audio version of this article
    Sponsored by
    0:00 / 2:40
    Instaread

    There’s really no place like Marin. Just click your heels together and presto, we have some of the best vistas in the world and more outdoor adventures than you can pack into one trip – all right at your fingertips.

    Slide Ranch is something you won’t want to miss – the ocean vistas are breathtaking and this hidden coastal gem hosts some of the coolest activities for you and the family.  Locals have known about it for years but for visitors it’s a wow-worthy discovery – a working organic farm tucked into the abundant beauty of the Golden Gate National Recreation area.  Bonus: it’s a prime spot for photos of the coast and the Golden Gate Bridge.

    Follow the winding road toward Muir Beach, and you’ll hit the Muir Beach Overlook. I never tire of the views from this spot. The walkway down opens into an unparalleled panorama of the coastline so bring your phone — you’ll want shots of the California coast and the Golden Gate Bridge – said to be the most photographed bridge in the world!

    There’s more to satisfy your craving for a view. Check out the Mountain Home Inn  on the slopes of Marin’s famous Mt. Tamalpais – locally known as “The Sleeping Lady” because its ridge profile resembles the silhouette of a reclining lady. Soak up some sun on the deck, order a drink and a bite, and gaze down into the enchanting town of Mill Valley, embraced by redwood trees. Consider an overnight stay at the Mt. Home Inn and explore the mountain’s many trails on the mountain where every turn brings another camera-ready moment including an Oz- like view of San Francisco, shimmering in the distance.

    Traveling north on the coast, you’ll pass Stinson Beach and on a clear day, you’ll see the Farallon Islands (25 miles offshore) and the Point Reyes peninsula stretching out like a slender finger into the Pacific. The drive to Pt. Reyes Station is one of my favorite scenic routes – and once you’re there ask a local how to find the Pt Reyes Lighthouse in the Pt. Reyes National Seashore. You won’t regret it.

    Lodging in the Pt Reyes area is a real treat. Nick’s Cove Tomales Bay pairs rustic charm with luxurious comfort and calm outdoor activities from stand up paddle boarding to bocce ball.  The restaurant, bar, and cottages set the stage for a serene seaside escape!  And one of our favorite local secrets, is Apple Garden Cottage in Tomales.  Just the name alone is food for the soul. This private bed-and-breakfast sits on a working farm. Did I hear you say “romantic” getaway?
